intro: Freight broker cold email is your primary tool for turning cold leads into active shippers. You spend hours crafting messages, but if you do not have a structured approach, you are just adding noise to a crowded inbox.

blocks.text: Why your freight broker cold email campaigns fail
Most brokers treat email as a transaction. You send a rate sheet. You wait. You send another email asking if they saw the first one. This is not prospecting. It is spamming.

Shippers are inundated with emails from brokers. If your message does not offer immediate value, it gets deleted. The problem is often that you are focusing on your own needs, not the shipper's pain points.
The high cost of manual prospecting

When you manually type every email, you lose focus. You spend 50 percent of your day on sales tasks. If you are also managing loads, you are likely burning out. This leads to inconsistent follow-ups. You stop emailing after two tries. But the data shows it often takes 8 to 12 touchpoints to get a response.
How to fix your outreach without new software

items: Create a template library in Gmail. Use Settings > Advanced to enable Templates.
Focus your message on market intelligence. Share a trend you saw on FreightWaves SONAR.
Use a consistent cadence. Send an email, wait two days, then send a follow-up with a new piece of data.
Keep your subject lines short. Use the company name and a specific lane or commodity.
Always include a clear call to action. Ask for a specific time to talk, not just a general check-in.

blocks.text: If you are using a Mac, use ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to summarize your last five emails with a prospect. This helps you identify where the conversation stalled.
blocks.title: Use your Mac to review progress

blocks.text: You do not need an expensive CRM to start. Use Google Sheets to track your outreach. Create columns for the last touchpoint, the next action, and the prospect's industry. Use your browser to keep everything in one place.
Common mistakes in freight broker cold email

items: Sending the same generic template to 100 people at once.
Forgetting to include the shipper's specific lane needs.
Giving up after the second email.
Using complex language that obscures your actual value proposition.
Failing to track which emails actually get a reply.

faq.question: How many emails should I send to a prospect?
faq.answer: Aim for 8 to 12 touchpoints. Most brokers give up too early. Use a mix of email, phone, and LinkedIn to keep the relationship warm.

faq.question: Is it worth using AI to write my emails?
faq.answer: Yes, but keep it human. Use AI to draft the structure or research the prospect's company, then edit it to sound like you.

faq.question: What is the best time to send cold emails?
faq.answer: Early morning or mid-afternoon usually works best. Avoid Monday mornings when everyone is clearing out their weekend backlog.
